answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether it sells velvet, onyx, or umber pigment. The bond stays locked while the identity is active and for 30 days after exit. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating a thousand sellers requires a thousand bonds. An attacker must tie up real capital for every fake seller, sacrificing liquidity and investment returns even if none is caught misbehaving.
